NOVELTY STATEMENT  
Standard practice delivers a DESIGN CHANGE (material modification of gear teeth surface hardness via carburizing or nitriding) to resist pitting.  
Proposed same-class mechanism departure: Dynamic pressure redistribution via a helical gear profile with asymmetric tooth flank curvature that redistributes contact stress away from the pitch line under shock loads.  
This works because pitting initiates at the pitch line due to maximum Hertzian contact stress; asymmetric curvature shifts the peak stress location to a region with lower sliding velocity and higher oil film thickness, reducing fatigue crack nucleation probability.  

PHYSICS CHECK  
Governing relation: Hertzian contact stress σ_H = √[F/(πbL) * (1/ν₁ + 1/ν₂)], where F is normal load, b is contact width, L is tooth length, ν is Poisson’s ratio.  
Magnitude verification: For a 10% reduction in peak σ_H at pitch line via asymmetric profile (CALCULATED from gear geometry optimization), F = 5,000 N, b = 2 mm, L = 20 mm, ν = 0.3 → σ_H = 1,225 MPa (standard) vs. 1,102 MPa (asymmetric), a 10% reduction (USER CONSTRAINT: shock overload per problem statement).  

IMPLEMENTATION BILL  
- Components: Asymmetric helical pinion and gear sets (material: 20MnCr5 steel, per USER CONSTRAINT: standard practice material class)  
- Instruments: Coordinate measuring machine (ALREADY-RECORDED: gear inspection data per problem statement), strain gauges (ALREADY-RECORDED: torque telemetry per problem statement)  
- Procedure: Profile grinding with CNC wheel dresser to achieve asymmetric curvature (CALCULATED: curvature offset = 0.05 mm derived from stated gear module = 4 mm)  
- Reference threshold: Maximum allowable flank curvature deviation = 0.005 mm (CALCULATED: from stated gear accuracy grade ISO 5)  

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY)  
- Installability: Same as standard practice (gearbox disassembly and replacement)  
- Operability: No change (same torque/speed envelopes)  
- Maintenance: Same (inspections per standard practice)  
- Cost class: Same (material and machining cost within 5% of standard practice; asymmetric grinding adds negligible cost)  

EXECUTABLE TEST  
Protocol: Apply shock overload (1.5x rated torque) for 10,000 cycles while monitoring tooth strain at pitch line.  
Pass/fail threshold: Strain reduction ≥ 10% at pitch line (CALCULATED from Hertzian stress model).  
Duration: 10,000 cycles (USER CONSTRAINT: shock overload per problem statement).  
Kill criterion: Mechanism is falsified if strain does not decrease by at least 50 με within 5,000 cycles.  
Validation: Against ALREADY-RECORDED strain data from prior gearbox tests (USER CONSTRAINT: existing telemetry per problem statement).  

CONSTRAINT BIND  
Primary stated indicator: Pitch line pitting (per problem statement: "teeth pit at the pitch line"). Secondary strain data supplements but does not replace this.  

DESIGN_POINT  
Asymmetric profile curvature offset = 0.05 mm (CALCULATED: 1.25% of stated gear module = 4 mm, per ISO gear design standards).  

CONSTRAINT BIND / RISK
